Coordination primitives (Brief/Assign/Evidence/Review) - only protocol defining how agents work together on tasks
Beneficiary attribution with Merkle proofs - no competitor traces value to human principals
Values Floor with cryptographic attestation - no competitor has constitutional ethical principles
Cross-agent Ed25519 verification proven live across 3 runtimes and models
Signed evidence chains in multi-agent coordination - this analysis is itself the proof
competitors_have_we_lack: Enterprise IdP bridging (Predicate) - no Okta/Entra/OIDC integration
DLP scanning (AIP/OAI) - we verify scope but dont scan response content
Visa-scale commerce integration - no payment rail
HITL approval workflows (AIP) - no native human-gate for specific actions
gapAnalysis.closest_competitor: OpenAgentIdentityProtocol (AIP) is closest. MCP proxy, policy enforcement, active spec. But fundamentally a PROXY not a PROTOCOL. They enforce tool-call rules. We define agent relationships - identity, delegation, coordination, governance. AIP is Layer 2 without Layers 1, 3-7. Their own spec acknowledges Layer 1 identity is IN PROGRESS - which is what we built.

positioningRecommendation: The Agent Passport System is the only protocol that treats agent coordination as a first-class concern - not just identity or policy, but the full stack from who are you to who authorized you to who benefits to how do you work together. Every competitor solves one slice: Visa solves commerce auth, AIP solves tool-call policy, Predicate solves enterprise authorization, clawdentity solves cross-platform identity. We solve the whole problem - and prove it by using our own protocol to coordinate the agents that built this analysis. Ship the How It Compares page with this evidence chain as proof: not a feature checklist but a live multi-agent workflow that competitors cannot replicate.
